clue.text: Brute roams wild in botanical gardens

indicators.note: running wild, the letters of the two words are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug runs riot among the flowerbeds of a public garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboretums are tree collections laid out as botanical gardens, a plural for a plural.

clue.text: Sailor heading off on journey in ship

indicators.note: the sailor word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
a go can be a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A seaman sets out on a voyage aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' strips the T from TAR, leaving AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary vessel of Jason and the Argonauts, so a famous example of a ship.

clue.text: Generous, keeping nothing in personal account

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it, as a container keeps its contents

parts.note: big-hearted, so big means generous
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A big-hearted person keeps nothing back in a private record.
explanation.definitionFit: A biog is short for biography, a written account of a person's life.

clue.text: Lowest possible cost of jam and cereal for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner is famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: jam is a fruit preserve
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A shopper looks for the cheapest price on jam and breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening PR of PRESERVE with the R of RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: At auction a reserve price is the minimum the seller will accept, the lowest possible selling cost.

clue.text: Accent in The Sound of Music?

definitions.meaning: a nasal regional way of speaking, as in a Southern drawl
the ringing note of a plucked string, playfully the musical film's title

explanation.surface: Someone detects a regional accent in the famous musical film.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is really a description of a plucked guitar string's sound; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is both a nasal accent and the vibrating sound of a plucked string.

clue.text: Tom Thumb was a fighter

definitions.meaning: the tiny folk-tale hero, playfully a very small man
an American militiaman of the Revolutionary War, ready at a minute's notice

explanation.surface: The tiny folk hero turns out to have been a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'minute' as tiny for Tom Thumb; Minutemen were colonial militia ready to fight at a minute's notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuteman was a US colonial militia soldier, and minute (tiny) man describes Tom Thumb.

clue.text: Complain vehicle has very little power

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the abbreviation for power, a single letter being a tiny share of it

explanation.surface: A motorist grumbles that their car is underpowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble, a synonym of complain.

clue.text: Was sorry a game plan ultimately proved deficient, when drawn up

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: in a down answer, drawing up lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
the plan word is found lacking at its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: a design is a plan

explanation.surface: Someone apologises because their game plan failed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately proved deficient' cuts DESIGN to DESIG; 'when drawn up' turns that to GISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have apologised is to have expressed that one was sorry.

clue.text: Old man's ailing more having swallowed liquid form of medicine

indicators.note: the outer pieces take the liquid down inside them

parts.note: pa is a father, the old man
iller is ailing to a greater degree
ink is a liquid

explanation.surface: An ailing father swallows a liquid dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is an analgesic, one form of medicine.

clue.text: Shiny coat, note, mislaid when touring part of Europe

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: the word for mislaid goes round the country, as a tourist would

parts.note: something mislaid is lost
Spain is a country in Europe

explanation.surface: A traveller loses a note while touring Europe, over a glossy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of Europe' could be any country; SPAIN fits because the mislaid word wraps around it, as a tourist goes round a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss paint is a high-shine finish, a shiny coat for woodwork.

clue.text: Half-heartedly catch single fish

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters, half the heart, is dropped

parts.note: a hook is a catch, as on a door
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: An angler half-heartedly catches one fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one O from the heart of HOOK, leaving HOK.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoki is a New Zealand food fish of the hake family.

clue.text: First of novices that is entering in nunnery is troublesome

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters go into the nunnery word

parts.note: a convent is a nunnery
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A new arrival entering a nunnery causes trouble for the novices.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient causes difficulty, so it is troublesome.

clue.text: British PC having to face the music — that's novel

parts.note: politically correct means right-on
rock is a kind of music

explanation.surface: A British police constable has to face the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable but means politically correct, RIGHT-ON; BRIGHTON ROCK is Graham Greene's novel (also a seaside candy stick).
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is a 1938 novel by Graham Greene.

clue.text: Eventually finds line's out of action

parts.note: a track is a railway line, with the 's as is
a system that is down is out of action

explanation.surface: A railway line has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down someone is to find them after searching, eventually locating them.

clue.text: Removes skin around fish for youngsters

indicators.note: the stripping word goes round the fish

parts.note: to strip is to peel off a covering
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone skins a fish to feed the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Striplings are adolescent youths, youngsters.

clue.text: Went off, crossing river west of American city

indicators.note: in an across answer, west of means placed before
the word for went off spans the river letter

parts.note: food that went off rotted

explanation.surface: Something went rotten while crossing a river west of an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major Dutch port city.

clue.text: Appreciate European renouncing a drug

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it

indicators.note: giving up the a, one letter is dropped

parts.note: an Italian is a European

explanation.surface: A European appreciates giving up a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renouncing' takes an A out of ITALIAN, leaving ITALIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalin is a heart drug extracted from foxglove.

clue.text: Loiter about, wasting time in bay

indicators.note: the remaining letters are turned about into a new order
the time letter is thrown away

explanation.surface: Someone hangs around a bay, wasting time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' removes T from LOITER; 'about' rearranges LOIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a projecting bay window.

clue.text: Court official, one mediating between councillor and monarch

indicators.note: the one stands between the two others as a mediator would

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A court official mediates between a councillor and the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A crier makes public announcements in a court of law, a court official.

clue.text: Information I've circulated to one woman and another

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the letters are passed around into a new order

parts.note: Eve is another woman's name

explanation.surface: Information I have circulated goes to a couple of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevieve is a woman's name, so one woman.

clue.text: "France-gites": new organisation raking in pounds for such a holiday?

indicators.note: taking in money, the anagram holds the pounds letter
the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A French gites company reorganises and makes money from holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new organisation' rearranges FRANCEGITES; 'raking in' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-catering holiday is one where guests cook their own meals, such as in a gite.

clue.text: Lift beams, say

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so it sounds like another

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone lifts beams.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: raising a flag or a glass means hoisting it upwards, exactly as lifting does.

clue.text: Where you'll hear loud song?

parts.note: f is forte, loud in music
an air is a song

explanation.surface: A question about where one hears loud singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is noisy with loud music.

clue.text: Absolutely dull

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb means completely, as in ... right

explanation.definitionFit: Dead means completely (dead certain) and also lifeless or dull.

clue.text: Beastly noise emanating from zoo in Kenya

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words

explanation.surface: A noise comes from an animal in a Kenyan zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: An oink is a pig's grunt, the noise of a beast.

clue.text: I will say a number of times: 27?

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone vows to repeat themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to read, so poorly educated; synonym of the answer at 27.

clue.text: Home established at end of garden?

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A home is set up at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: birds build and live in a nest, so it serves as their home.

clue.text: Poorly educated and characterless?

definitions.meaning: having no letters, letters being characters

explanation.definitionFit: Unlettered means illiterate and, cryptically, without characters.
